title: Pohutukawa: New Zealand Christmas Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: New Zealand's Christmas tree flowers scarlet in Iberia in early summer, half a year off schedule. Five pohutukawa mapped in Portugal and Cadiz.
intro: New Zealand's Christmas tree does its flowering here in early summer. Metrosideros excelsa covers itself in scarlet brushes at the height of the southern summer, which in Cadiz, Lisbon, Porto and Sintra falls half a year off its native schedule and a hemisphere from home. At home it grows on sea cliffs, gripping rock with aerial roots, which is close to what the Atlantic edge of Iberia offers it. The Monserrate tree in Sintra is the oldest of the five, though nobody will pin it closer than somewhere between 175 and 275 years. Porto's pair on the grass at Passeio Alegre stand eleven metres apart and are barely taller than a house. Lisbon's two, in the Jardim da Parada, are ten metres apart and protected as separate trees. Five are mapped, four in Portugal and one in Cadiz.
